updates.title: AWS Quick packages agents and integrations as plugins
updates.whatChanged: AWS Quick now offers plugins on 21 November. Users can browse more than 100 official plugins or describe a job so Quick assembles a custom plugin from agents, skills, connectors and flows. Teams can share custom plugins within their organization.
updates.whyCare: You can deploy a repeatable role or task bundle instead of assembling agents and integrations for each team. Compare the plugin package with your current Quick workspace and approval patterns.
updates.before: AWS Quick users assembled agents, skills, connectors and flows as separate workspace capabilities.
updates.after: Quick can distribute an installable plugin that bundles these capabilities for a task or role.
updates.learn: Pilot a plugin on one routine job. Check connector permissions, shared credentials and owner reviews before you distribute it widely.

sources.name: AWS What's New - AWS Quick plugins

updates.architectureImplication: Treat plugins as versioned distribution units for agent behavior, integrations and workflow steps. Define ownership and approval at the plugin boundary.
heldReasons: Fact check: More than 100 official plugins are available to browse. | The source says there are more than 100 skills and plugins in total, but it does not state that more than 100 official plugins are available.

Fact check: AWS Quick users previously assembled agents, skills, connectors and flows as separate workspace capabilities. | The source describes plugins and the bundle's current use, but says nothing about the previous workspace behavior.
